#1846. Barnsley vs Aldershot Town - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sam Varley | 05 Nov 2026 22:18, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 09:00

Aldershot Town will set out to pull off an FA Cup first-round upset in South Yorkshire on Saturday, when they visit Oakwell to take on third-tier Barnsley.

The hosts enter at this stage while their visitors took part in the final qualifying round and needed a replay to progress.

Barnsley head into FA Cup action for the first time this season on Saturday in need of a victory to arrest a slump in the early stages of 2026-27.

The Reds reached the third round of this competition last year, falling in a trip to Liverpool, but begin their new campaign with just four wins from 17 competitive matches so far this term with all of those coming in the first six outings.

They did enjoy a positive start to life back under returning boss Daniel Stendel but are now winless in 11 games since early September, losing nine of those including four straight league defeats heading into the weekend.

Stendel's men were, at least, able to end that rut at home to Oxford United on Saturday, drawing 1-1 thanks to Vimal Yoganathan's opener having been down to 10 men inside 10 minutes, but the South Yorkshire side still sit 23rd in League One with just nine points on the board from 12 games having conceded 22 goals.

With positives to take from the weekend's display but real cause for concern around their recent months, Barnsley will be desperate to avoid an upset at the weekend and taste victory at Oakwell.

Their opponents, meanwhile, make the trip north having scraped through the final qualifying round in the FA Cup.

Aldershot Town entered this year's competition in the fourth and final round of qualifying, taking on ninth-tier Tadley Calleva, but they were only able to draw 2-2 at home before prevailing in a 2-0 triumph on the road in the replay.

That eventual cup win broke up a five-game losing run in the National League for the Shots, who also headed into the weekend in the midst of a rut, but they bounced back to winning ways at home to Gateshead, as Brody Peart scored the only goal inside five minutes.

Scott Davies's side climbed back up to 14th spot in the fifth tier with that result, and now on the back of a midweek National League Cup loss to Ipswich Town Under-21s, they will hope to defy the odds at Oakwell on Saturday to reach the FA Cup second round for just the second time since 2015.

Barnsley are set to remain without attackers Ben Hamed Toure and Fabio Jalo on Saturday due to ongoing injuries.

Stendel should field a near full-strength XI with the Reds desperate for a win to turn their fortunes round, meaning star man Reyes Cleary should continue on the wing, while Tobi Adeyemo was injured early on Saturday and may be replaced up front by Rylan Brownlie.

Veteran and recent signing Daniel Johnson may be afforded a start in midfield alongside either Luca Connell or Patrick Kelly, while Jack Shepherd is available at the back despite being sent off last time out in the league.

Aldershot Town will field a similar starting XI from last week's league win over Gateshead.

Marcus Dinanga and Marcus Wyllie will both hope to start in attack, but if they continue with a 4-2-3-1 shape the line should again be led by Tristan Abrahams, who has scored six goals so far this season.

A summer of plenty of change added several key men to their ranks, with Michael Stickland and Kiki Oshilaja now mainstays in defence and Dominic Odusanya and Conor Lawless likely to continue a midfield partnership if the latter is fit having been forced off last weekend.

Slicker; Kay, Gale, Shepherd, Larkeche; Connell, Johnson; Yoganathan, McGeegan, Cleary; Brownlie

Hayes; Stickland, Oshilaja, Dyce, Harfield; Lawless, Odusanya; Peart, Tuma, Sandah; Abrahams

Barnsley could certainly be vulnerable to a cup upset at home, given their poor league record and struggles at both ends of the pitch and growing concern around the club, but needing a win to start turning their form around, we do expect Stendel's men to outclass their non-league visitors.

#1845. The Man Utd change Michael Carrick must make against Aston Villa to keep his job

With JJ Gabriel almost out the door at Old Trafford Manchester United, and Michael Carrick will now be tempted to pin all their hopes on another emerging star in Shea Lacey.

The 19-year-old has played himself into first-team contention after a dazzling display off the bench in Tuesday’s comeback victory over Roma in the Champions League.

While it was Bruno Fernandes’ penalty that sparked the revival and Matheus Cunha’s brace that got them over the line, Lacey’s fearless cameo on the right was the catalyst for change.

Even the perennially reserved Michael Carrick couldn’t hide his delight over the performance, noting the teenager has ‘that bit of mischief’ in his locker that troubled Roma for the final 15 minutes of the game. Lacey ended the contest playing in defence after Cunha’s red card with Carrick jokingly christening him his new right-back.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Lacey’s sharp, perfectly-weighted passing enabled United to get up the pitch with real intent – seldom seen this season. He completed every one of his attempted passes and completed all but one of his duels. Operating in tight spaces just in front of the touchline, his first touches and clever exchanges were on point from the moment he came on. His pass for Cunha’s winner couldn’t have been placed better.

It has been a long time coming for Lacey. Injuries shelved tentative plans for him to make his debut at 16 under Erik ten Hag in 2023 and it was a tough road back from those issues that threatened to halt his progress.

‘Everybody in the world knows about Shea Lacey,’ United’s former Under-21 manager Travis Binnion said last year. ‘So he needs a little bit of fortune, he needs to be patient with himself and everybody else needs to be really patient with him.’ That patience could now be about to pay off.

Whether Tuesday’s win was a turning point or another false dawn for United remains to be seen. Jose Mourinho and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer led United to delirium-inducing comeback victories over Newcastle United in Atalanta with identical scorelines when the pressure was mounting on their shoulders. Both were gone shortly after.

But with Carrick’s back against the wall, there is the opportunity to roll the dice with Lacey. The Liverpool-born talent thumped home a wonderful strike in the Carabao Cup defeat to Brighton but has seen just 31 minutes of action off the bench since. Excluding the second-half performance against Roma, United’s attack has lacked any verve or real invention. A change is needed and Lacey will feel this is his chance.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

It was on the right where he caused damage midweek with Amad Diallo making way for him after 75 minutes. It had been another disappointing evening for the Ivory Coast international who spurned huge opportunities against Chelsea four days earlier.

Since forcing his way back into the side under Erik ten Hag, Amad has been looked upon as United’s most naturally talented winger. But his goal and assist return has fallen woefully short of expectations. He is now approaching one year without a goal, last finding the back of the net in the 4-4 draw with Bournemouth on 15 December. In that time, he has provided two assists – one on the final day of last season against Brighton and the other for Joshua Zirkzee’s consolation goal in the 4-1 humiliation in Como two weeks ago.

His haul of 14 goals during his magnificent campaign with Sunderland in the 2022-23 season is a distant memory. A hat-trick against Southampton in January 2025 helped him to an impressive haul of 11 goals and 10 assists in his first full campaign back in Manchester but seven goal involvements in 40 appearances since the start of the 2025-26 campaign is not good enough.

Wayne Rooney alluded to Amad’s problem midweek and made his case for Lacey getting the nod.

‘Amad does some really good things, but it’s that end product, that is what takes you to the next level,’ he told Amazon Prime. ‘And the glimpses of what I’ve seen from Lacey when he has come on…he has got something in there, that little touch and little pass which United needed to get them over the line in this game.’

The win over Roma has shifted a few clouds amid the gloom hanging over Old Trafford and Sunday’s visit of Aston Villa now looks a more inviting environment for Carrick to make the change and put his faith in Lacey.

#1844. Tottenham XI vs Leeds: Confirmed team news, predicted lineup and injury latest for Premier League

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Tottenham are set to be boosted by the returns of midfield duo Lucas Bergvall and Rodrigo Bentancur for Saturday’s trip to Leeds.

Bergvall has been out since suffering a knee injury against Manchester United at the start of October, while Bentancur is back after a three-game suspension served following his late dismissal in the same game at Old Trafford.

In the pair’s absence, Roberto De Zerbi has relied on Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes in midfield, and their performances over the last three games have given the Spurs boss plenty to think about.

Centre-back Tosin Adarabioyo is also expected to be back fit after missing the last two games through injury.

This weekend’s trip to Elland Road, where Spurs are looking to make it four wins in a row for the first time in more than 1,000 days, will come too soon for Mykhailo Mudryk, though.

Speaking ahead of Spurs’ 2-0 victory over Crystal Palace last weekend, De Zerbi confirmed that Mudryk and fellow winger Savio would not be back until after the international break, though the latter has been seen back with the squad at Hotspur Way this week.

"Before the international break, for Tosin and Bergvall. Maybe," De Zerbi said. "Maybe not from the beginning against Leeds, but available, yes, I hope so. Mudryk and Savio, after the international break."

James Maddison was not risked against Palace following a groin issue suffered in the win over Chelsea, and should therefore be available to play some part at Leeds, while Wilson Odobert and Xavi Simons remain long-term absentees.

However, there have been reports this week that Simons is now entering the final stage of his recovery from an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) rupture suffered back in April and is expected back in training later in November, well ahead of schedule.

De Zerbi was able to provide a positive recent update on Odobert, suggesting that he could be back training in January after tearing his ACL in February.

"(He should be back in training) after December,” De Zerbi said. “After Christmas. In January, I think. It is a great thing for us.”

Pedro Porro was named among the substitutes against Palace, but should be fit enough to start at Leeds.

Destiny Udogie, though, needs more time before he is ready to return to the starting lineup, having not trained consistently since the September international break.

Varela was deemed surplus to requirements at Benfica and moved to newly promoted Italian outfit Monza for a fee of just €2million (£1.7m) – plus performance-related bonuses – in the summer.

Monza are languishing down in 18th place in the table, with only two wins to their name, in what has been a difficult start to life on their return to Serie A.

Varela has proven a shining light up front, though, scoring nine goals in his opening nine appearances, and his barnstorming form in Lombardy has begun to attract the attentions of European football’s elite.

It’s claimed Arsenal are among a host of Premier League clubs to have ‘expressed an interest’ in Varela and ‘one of the first to enquire’ about the player’s potential availability.

#1842. Manchester United XI vs Aston Villa: Confirmed team news, predicted lineup, injury latest for Premier League

Manchester United will be hoping to welcome back a couple of stars when they welcome Aston Villa to Old Trafford on Sunday.

The Red Devils put a stop to their winless run on Tuesday with a dramatic 3-2 victory over Roma in the Champions League.

Matheus Cunha netted a late brace to turn the game on its head, with the hosts looking a beaten side at half time.

They turned things around in the second half when Bruno Fernandes tucked away a penalty at the second attempt, before Cunha was on hand to lash home with five minutes to play and secure a valuable three points for under-fire manager Michael Carrick.

Carrick had been under serious scrutiny following United’s worst ever start to a Premier League campaign, with his side languishing in 17th in the top-flight table.

Now, however, they will be looking to build some momentum after a much-needed win.

There could be returns for Marcus Rashford and Patrick Dorgu from injury, with the former on the comeback trail of a hip problem, while the latter was a surprise returner to training from a hamstring issue picked up on international duty.

As such, it could hand Carrick a more natural option at left-back, with Diogo Dalot filling in in that position in recent games.

By Sam Varley | 05 Nov 2026 22:29

Aiming to continue their climb up the Championship table and break into the playoff places, Sheffield United will head to The Valley to take on Charlton Athletic on Saturday.

Back-to-back victories have seen the visitors move within a point of the top eight, while their visitors sit four points above the drop zone after four straight losses.

Charlton Athletic return to action at the weekend aiming to end a dismal run of Championship form and arrest a drop towards the relegation zone.

Following a 19th-placed finish in their first season back in the second tier last time around, the Addicks won their first three league matches of the new term but have since drawn five and lost six of 11 matches.

In those games, Nathan Jones's side have scored just six goals and conceded 20, dropping to 21st spot in the process, just one place and four points above Burnley in the drop zone.

They have now suffered four straight defeats heading into their final match before the international break, falling to Watford, Norwich City and Middlesbrough before they hosted newly-promoted Bolton Wanderers on Tuesday and again came away empty-handed as Sam Dalby scored the only goal inside 20 minutes at the Valley.

With pressure surely growing on Jones, and the international break arguably coming at a decent time to arrest Charlton's slump, they will be desperate to put a win on the board to increase their lead over the drop zone ahead of the return to action.

Their visitors, meanwhile, head to London aiming to carry an upturn in form into the break.

Unlike the hosts, Sheffield United are now bouncing back from a slow start to the Championship season, having set out to challenge for promotion this term only to pick up just nine points from their first eight matches before the opening break of the season.

Following a 1-0 home victory over Wrexham on Friday, the Blades headed to strugglers Preston North End on Tuesday and came from 1-0 down to win 3-2 thanks to Sydie Peck's first-half hat-trick, leaving them on 22 points from 14 matches with just five teams conceding fewer than the 17 goals they have allowed.

Now in a much better position in ninth spot, and just one point behind eighth-placed West Ham United, Sheffield United will look to make it three straight wins with the chance to head into the second break of the campaign in the playoff places.

Sheffield United are without forwards Patrick Bamford and Ryan One and midfielder Joe Rothwell, while Kalvin Phillips was also absent in midweek but may be fit to feature.

He is unlikely to be rushed back, though, and Wilder should field a similar starting XI from their midweek away win, meaning Jairo Riedewald may again partner Peck, who decided that game with his hat-trick, while Liam Kitching should come straight back into the defence after serving a one-match suspension on Tuesday.

In a 4-4-2 shape, they may again be flanked by Romelle Donovan and Tahith Chong with Ben Brereton Diaz, Tom Cannon, Tyrese Campbell and Oliver Arblaster competing for attacking spots in Bamford's absence.

#1838. GdS: Milan search for ‘spark’ in Europe – how Amorim plans to harness post-derby ‘fuel’

After beating Inter in the derby on Saturday night, AC Milan are hoping that they can ride the wave and get back on track in Europe.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) write that Milan want to rediscover their ‘international DNA’ and put behind them a start to the Europa League campaign that has seen one win and two defeats in the first three games.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

While it is not yet a do-or-die situation for Ruben Amorim and his squad, failing to secure a win against the Hungarian side – who have a perfect record so far – would make reaching the top 24 significantly more difficult, and a top-eight finish nearly impossible.

Given that the Rossoneri have won seven Champions League titles, no other team in this European competition can boast such a trophy cabinet. Furthermore, the Portuguese manager reached the final with Manchester United two editions ago, ultimately losing to Tottenham.

Consequently, Milan and Amorim must ‘honour’ the Europa League in a manner far removed from their last away outing, which was a heavy defeat against European debutants Bournemouth, with Mike Maignan getting sent off.

This evening over 50,000 fans are expected at San Siro, including a sold-out away sector of 4,200, with over 5,000 Hungarian fans in total throughout the stadium. Milan must secure a victory, channelling the enthusiasm currently felt at Milanello following Saturday’s derby win.

The former United manager tried to brush it aside so his squad could focus solely on the Europa League, but the atmosphere during the final training session was as upbeat as it gets, with lots of ‘slaps’ of congratulations dished out.

Koni De Winter was patted on the back in celebration of his daughter’s birth, Diego Moreira was praised for his goal in the derby, Sankhoun Diawara was acknowledged for his debut(s), and even coach Carlos Fernandes got some love for the corner routine leading to Adrien Rabiot’s goal.

😂 A lot of slaps were given out before training: De Winter for the birth of his daughter, Pulisic for his renewal, Diawara for his debut and Carlos Fernandes for the corner routine leading to Rabiot’s goal ❤️🖤

— SempreMilan (@SempreMilanCom) November 4, 2026

The enthusiasm following the derby must now be channelled into focus and determination ahead of the Europa League return. Milan cannot afford another embarrassing performance in European competition, like those seen against Benfica and Bournemouth.

The club’s storied history forbids it, and Gerry Cardinale certainly wouldn’t welcome a repeat of those displays against the Portuguese or English sides. For this reason, while rotating the squad with an eye on Sunday’s match in Genoa, Amorim will ensure the team retains some key pillars.

De Winter will remain in defence, Yunus Musah and Rabiot in midfield, and Goncalo Ramos in attack. Compared to Saturday’s lineup, there will be seven changes including a forced one in goal, with Lorenzo Torriani replacing the suspended Maignan. Ardon Jashari steps in for Luka Modrić, who will be rested.

With six players sidelined due to injury, the scope for rotation is limited. Yet, even while fielding a side with a significantly lower average age than the one that played in the derby (23.6 years versus 28.1), Amorim has opted not to throw 18-year-olds Francesco Camarda and Christian Comotto into the XI.

His goal is to help Gonçalo Ramos – who hasn’t managed a single shot on target in his last two appearances – regain his scoring touch. Consequently, Camarda will have to wait a little longer. As for Comotto, the midfield requires experience, and both Rabiot and Musah are too vital to be left out.

Across the 2024-25 Champions League and the current Europa League campaign, the Rossoneri have won only one of their last six matches, hardly the kind of record expected from a club with such a storied continental past.

According to UEFA, a win in the Europa League is worth €450,000 (with €150,000 for a draw), figures that pale in comparison to the rewards for similar results in the Champions League (€2.1m and €700k, respectively).

The total earnings at the end of each competition are also incomparable: Champions League finalists can rake in between €120m and €125m, whereas the winner of the Europa League can earn, at most, just over €40m.

However, securing the second-tier European trophy guarantees direct qualification for the 2027-28 Champions League, bypassing the need to finish in the top four of Serie A. It also grants a spot in the UEFA Super Cup, which awards €4m to each of the two participating clubs.

Returning to the Champions League – a major objective that was not achieved last season – must be achieved this year, not least for the sake of sponsorships and brand value, two areas of great importance to Cardinale.

Ultimately, the goal is to win a trophy, ideally the Scudetto. However, adding the Europa League title to the trophy cabinet would certainly be a welcome achievement, especially given Milan didn’t win it when it was the UEFA Cup either.

#1837. Spalletti: Juventus should be given credit for every Europa League win

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Luciano Spalletti claimed Juventus should be given credit no matter who they beat in the Europa League, while saying his side showed courage against AZ.

Juventus continued their unbeaten start to their Europa League campaign with a 2-1 victory away to AZ, keeping them in the mix at the top of the table after four games.

Teun Koopmeiners and Randal Kolo Muani scored their goals in the first half, and Juventus held on for all three points despite Mexx Meerdink's late consolation.

Juve (11 goals in this Europa League) have scored more than 10 goals after the first four matches of a season in major European competition for the first time since 1999-2000 (14 in UEFA Cup).

And they have 10 points on the board at the halfway stage, having also beaten NEC (5-0) and Celta Vigo (2-1) earlier in the league phase.

Juventus were the favourites ahead of their clash with AZ and expected to win, but Spalletti pointed out that things are not always that simple out on the pitch.

"I am very satisfied, because we played well against a very strong team," Spalletti told Sky Sport Italia.

"I remember when all of you laughed in my face when we beat NEC 5-0; you acted as if they were a ridiculous team, but NEC now have seven points in the Europa League.

"So perhaps people need to re-evaluate how they consider us, humility, and giving credit to a team without just constantly wanting to put pressure on.

"When we win a game, people act as if it was because the opponents were weak, or finding some excuses. We played a strong game against a great team, and as we saw the moment our intensity dropped, they will take advantage.

FT | | Three more #UEL points! #AZJuve https://t.co/KQiJHOjZU9

— JuventusFC (@juventusfcen) November 5, 2026

"We've seen in the Champions League and Europa League, these sides might have a predictable way of doing things, but it becomes a strength when they can do it that many times.

"It is constantly hammering away at those situations; we were pinned back, worried about whether or not to push out from defence, and a through ball caused a goal.

"There were mad scrambles; if the game lasted for another three or four minutes, I don't think we would've taken the result home."

Juventus were largely in control, despite the hosts having double the number of shots (18 for AZ, nine for Juve). Both finished with three attempts on target apiece, however.

AZ also accumulated 2.2 expected goals (xG) to Juventus' 0.6 as they piled on the pressure towards the end, but Spalletti noted it was more important for his side to improve their attacking threat than how they defended a lead.

"What we needed to do was score a third goal," he added. "The way we played, we had to score a third goal there.

"When you win away to a team that hasn't lost at home in 17 European games, winning 14 of them, that is a sign you played with authority and quality. We showed the right courage."

#1836. Minnesota United vs San Jose Earthquakes - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Ojele | 05 Nov 2026 22:31, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 09:18

Minnesota United and San Jose Earthquakes draw the curtain on their 2026 Major League Soccer regular season campaign when they lock horns at Allianz Field on Sunday morning.

While the home side head into the league finale needing maximum points to stand a chance of securing back-to-back playoff appearances, San Jose will aim to finish the campaign strong and gather momentum ahead of the post-season quest.

A strong showing at the business end of the season has put Minnesota United in contention for playoff qualification ahead of a crunch final-day showdown, with the Loons securing a 3-1 win over Los Angeles FC on Monday to maintain their newfound form.

Joaquin Pereyra turned in an eye-catching display at the BMO Stadium, netting on either side of Cherrion Valerius’s 34th-minute strike to put the visitors three goals up, before Sergio Vasquez pulled one back for Los Angeles FC in the 89th minute.

Coming off a 3-1 victory over Sporting Kansas City on October 29, Minnesota United have now picked up three wins in their most recent four outings and are unbeaten in six straight matches (3W 3D), having lost each of the five games preceding this run.

This late-season resurgence has seen Cameron Knowles’s men surge into 12th place in the Western Conference standings with 41 points from 33 matches, just two points behind ninth-placed Colorado Rapids in the final playoff qualifying spot.

Attacking improvements have been integral in Minnesota’s upturn in form, with 2+ goals scored in five of their last six games, and they will also hope to make home advantage count against an opposing side who have failed to win their last six league visits to Allianz Field, losing four and claiming two draws since a 3-1 victory in May 2018.

Having seen their form take a dip in recent weeks, San Jose Earthquakes finally rediscovered their winning touch last Saturday when they held on to see out a 2-1 victory over Real Salt Lake and record their first victory since late September.

In an action-packed first half at PayPal Park, Ousseni Bouda and Benjamin Kikanovic netted in a 15-minute spell to put the Quakes in a commanding lead, and after Juan Sanabria halved the deficit with a 23rd-minute strike, the home side did well to repel Real Salt Lake and leave with all three points.

Prior to that, San Jose saw their nine-game unbeaten league streak come to an end on October 25, when they were hammered 3-0 by FC Dallas at the Toyota Stadium, four days before playing out a 2-2 stalemate with Colorado Rapids on home turf.

After enduring a disappointing 2025 campaign that saw them finish 10th in the West and narrowly miss out on the playoffs, Bruce Arena’s men have enjoyed a significant turnaround this season, collecting 52 points from 33 games to sit third in the conference standings, three points behind second-placed Dallas.

With playoff qualification already assured, San Jose will be keen to finish the regular season on a high, but a run of just one win in eight matches since August suggests they still have work to do before the campaign concludes.

San Jose Earthquakes Major League Soccer form:

Experienced midfielder Wil Trapp has missed each of Minnesota United’s last three matches due to the MLS concussion protocol, and the 33-year-old will play no part in Sunday’s finale.

American youngster Kayne Rizvanovich was left out of the team list against Los Angeles FC last time out, and the 19-year-old goalkeeper is also expected to sit out this weekend's matchup.

Kelvin Yeboah has been a standout performer for Minnesota this season, and the Italian striker, who has racked up 18 goals and four assists in 29 league starts, will be one to keep an eye on.

San Jose Earthquakes will be without several players down the spine of the team, including Darius Johnson and Jonathan Gonzalez, who have been ruled out through injuries.

Nigerian forward Nonso Adimabua is currently recuperating from a muscle problem while DeJuan Jones continues his lengthy spell on the sidelines through an Achilles tendon injury.

Buoyed by their victory over Real Salt Lake, San Jose Earthquakes will head into the season finale in high spirits, but they have their work cut out against an in-form Minnesota United side who have their sights set on a top-nine finish.

However, San Jose’s form on the road leaves a lot to be desired, and we predict Minnesota will outscore Arena’s men this weekend and extend their impressive home record in this fixture.

#1835. Destiny Udogie: Tottenham star sent advice over 'problematic' injuries after Roberto De Zerbi admission

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Former Tottenham left-back Christian Ziege says Destiny Udogie must train consistently before returning to action or risk another injury setback.

Udogie made his first appearance in three weeks, coming off the bench to help Spurs see out a 2-0 win over 10-man Crystal Palace last weekend.

The 23-year-old has been struggling with a knee injury sustained at the start of October against Manchester United and has been in and out of full-team training.

Asked about Udogie’s persistent injury issues, Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi admitted they were becoming “problematic” and added that his minutes would remain limited so long as he was unable to train consistently.

Ziege, who made 55 appearances for Spurs between 2001 and 2004, agrees with De Zerbi and believes Udogie stands to suffer yet more injuries if he tries to return before training properly.

"If you see Destiny Udogie’s history over the last few months, he's had some problems with his knees and a few other issues. I don't know the exact reasons for that, but the most important thing if you want to be a real contender and play at the highest level is that you have to be fully fit when you come back,” Ziege exclusively tells Standard Sport on behalf of BOYLE Sports, who offer the latest football odds.

"If you're not fully fit, it can cause problems, because then you pick up another small, tiny injury. You can't reach your highest level if you haven't trained properly or aren't fully fit, and that leads to more problems.

"So my advice would always be to get really fit, get ready to play 90 minutes. That's the best thing you can do, otherwise, you'll face more setbacks than you deserve."

In Udogie’s absence, the experienced Andy Robertson has deputised ably, and Ziege says he is impressed by the left-back options De Zerbi has at his disposal.

"Spurs have great options at left-back, Andy Robertson has a lot of experience winning the Premier League, as well as the Champions League with Liverpool,” Ziege continued.

"So that's a massive signing, I think. Destiny Udogie is a bit of a different player. From my point of view, he's maybe got a bit more skill and is more offensive.

Young goalkeeper Mike Penders kept a clean sheet in that game as summer signing Martinez continued his recovery from surgery following the fractured jaw he suffered in last month’s victory against Everton.

But Martinez - wearing a protective face mask - was this week involved in Chelsea training at Cobham and could play on Wearside, depending on whether Xabi Alonso is keen to immediately reinstate his No1.

Alonso will provide the latest update on his Chelsea squad’s fitness and injury status when he holds his pre-match press conference on Friday afternoon.

Moises Caicedo was not spotted during the 15 minutes of Wednesday’s training session that was open to the media, but previously injured Argentine defender Aaron Anselmino was involved just a day after being selected to play for his country over the upcoming international window.

Alonso will be expected to provide clarity on the health of Jordan Henderson, who missed the win over United due to illness. Romeo Lavia started in his place and excelled so could keep his spot.

Estevao started against United and impressed so is another player who Alonso may find it difficult to bench.

Joao Pedro and Maxence Lacroix are both sidelined, along with Jorrel Hato and captain Reece James, who is recovering from knee surgery and unlikely to be available again until January.

Winger Jamie Gittens suffered an ankle injury on international duty with England’s Under-21s last month. He will be out for “a few weeks”, Alonso said a fortnight ago.

#1832. Andria Bartishvili injury: Arsenal's £4m signing suffers setback as statement issued on Instagram

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Andria Bartishvili, a future Arsenal player, will be sidelined for up to three months with an ankle injury.

The Gunners have already announced a pre-contract agreement for the 17-year-old, paying just under £4million to Georgian side Kolkheti 1913 and tying Bartishvili down to a five-year deal.

Under FIFA rules regarding youth transfers, Bartishvili cannot join Arsenal until he turns 18, explaining why the Gunners have to wait until next summer until the attacker arrives in north London.

Dubbed the ‘next Kvaratskhelia’ in reference to fellow countryman and Paris Saint-Germain star Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Bartishvili is currently on loan at Conference League outfit Iberia 1999 from Kolkheti 1913.

Like Kvaratskhelia, who faces a lengthy spell on the sidelines after rupturing his ACL against Barcelona last month, Bartishvili - as per reports in Georgia - has been ruled out for the remainder of 2026 after damaging ligaments in his right ankle while playing for Iberia 1999.

A statement on Instagram reads: “Andria Bartishvili’s MRI research has confirmed high-quality damage to the ATFL (Anterior Talo-Fibular Ligament).

“Andria will be able to complete several stages of treatment and complete rehabilitation before the end of the season.”

A product of the Dinamo Tbilisi academy, Bartishvili made his senior debut two days after his 16th birthday.

So far in 2026, the winger has grabbed two goals in 17 league appearances, while playing in two Conference League matches this season.

Currently 17, Bartishvili turns 18 in March 2027, after the January transfer window shuts and Arsenal reportedly beat out several top European clubs to capture the Georgian’s signature in September.

#1831. Dallas vs Colorado Rapids - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Ojele | 05 Nov 2026 22:48, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 09:14

Dallas and Colorado Rapids will look to close out the 2026 MLS regular season campaign on a strong note when they go head to head in the season finale at the Toyota Stadium on Sunday morning.

Both sides head into the game having something to play for, with the hosts in a two-man race with San Jose Earthquakes for second place in the Western Conference standings, while Colorado will be aiming to seal their spot in the playoffs.

Having finished 11th and seventh in the 2024 and 2025 MLS seasons respectively, Dallas have taken another significant step forward this term and are closing in on their highest conference finish since their 2016 title triumph.

With just eight clean sheets and 50 goals conceded in the league, improvements must be made at the back ahead of their post-season campaign, but Eric Quill’s men can take pride in their performance at the attacking end of the pitch, where they have netted a club record 59 goals so far.

Dallas' defensive shortcomings were on display last Saturday when they were held to a 1-1 draw by Sporting Kansas City at Children's Mercy Park, with Jansen Miller netting a 45th-minute equaliser to cancel out Herman Johansson’s 19th-minute opener and force a share of the spoils.

Having suffered a 2-1 defeat against Columbus Crew at the Toyota Stadium last Thursday, the Bulls have now dropped five points in their last two matches, with their recent dip in form dealing a significant blow to their hopes of securing the conference title.

Dallas head into the season finale with 15 wins and 10 draws from their 33 MLS matches to collect 55 points and sit second in the Western Conference standings, six points adrift of first-placed Vancouver Whitecaps.

Like the hosts, a slump in form at the business end of the season has threatened to derail Colorado Rapids’ campaign, with Matt Wells’s men dropping three more points in a 4-2 home defeat at the hands of Chicago Fire last Sunday.

Second-half strikes from Robert Lewandowski, Puso Dithejane, and a brace from Jonathan Bamba inspired Chicago Fire to all three points at Dick's Sporting Goods Park, with Morgan Whittaker and Paxten Aaronson getting on the scoresheet for the home side.

The Denver outfit have now failed to win eight of their most recent nine matches, losing three and claiming five draws, a run which saw them crash out of the US Open Cup in the semi-finals following a 3-0 defeat against St. Louis City on September 17.

Following their recent struggles, Saturday’s tie is a must-win for Colorado Rapids if they are to secure playoff qualification, as they sit ninth in the Western Conference standings, one point off seventh-placed LA Galaxy and two points above 12th-placed Minnesota United.

Colorado Rapids Major League Soccer form:

Logan Farrington has missed each of Dallas’ last five matches since sustaining an injury in October and the 24-year-old forward is out of contention for this weekend's finale.

He is joined on the club’s injury table by Brazilian defender Geovane Jesus, who continues his long road to full recovery from a severe knee injury.

With 22 goals under his belt, Petar Musa has been a standout performer for Dallas this season and the Croatian striker, who sits second in the league scoring charts, will look to deliver the goods once again.

Colorado Rapids have their fair share of injury concerns, with 28-year-old defender Reggie Cannon and the Ghanaian duo of Ali Fadal and Ibrahim Sadiq all ruled out of this weekend matchup.

Experienced goalkeeper Zack Steffen has been sidelined since May through a shoulder injury, while Frenchman Youssef Maziz has missed the last 10 games since sustaining a leg injury against Austin FC back in September.

Sirois; Johansson, Urhoghide, Ibeagha, Abubakar; Valiente, Kaick, Ramiro, Binyamin; Job, Moreno

Colorado Rapids possible starting lineup:

Defreitas-Hansen; Rosenberry, Holding, Williams, Navarro; Frederick, Whittaker, Ojediran; Aaronson, Yapi, Ku-DiPietro

Colorado Rapids find themselves in a heated six-team battle in the West for the three playoffs spots still up for grabs, but with just three points from eight games on the road, they are in for another tough 90 minutes at the Toyota Stadium.

Dallas have lost just one home game since August 6, and given Colorado’s away woes, we predict the Bulls’ quality across the pitch will see them emerge with all three points, killing off the visitors’ playoff dreams.

#1830. Le Bris urges Sunderland to ‘stick together and be combatitive to the end’

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Regis Le Bris conceded Sunderland are lacking confidence, but says the club and fans must "stick together and be combative until the end" after losing to Dinamo Zagreb.

Having gone unbeaten in their first three Europa League games this season (W2 D1), Sunderland suffered their first defeat on the continent, going down 2-0 to Dinamo.

Luka Stojkovic scored the opener before then teeing up Dion Beljo for their second before the break.

Wilson Isidor had a goal disallowed shortly after the break, and Sunderland twice hit the woodwork, but they failed to find a breakthrough as they slumped to defeat.

Le Bris is now coming under increasing pressure, with Sunderland also sitting bottom of the Premier League table after a disappointing start to the season.

And the Frenchman admitted their form is affecting their confidence across all competitions, not just in the top-flight.

When asked if they are out of confidence by TNT Sports, Le Bris said: "Probably.

"We have good players, a good team. I believe this team has a really big potential. We showed it last season. But you also have to experience tough situations. Last season, it happened a bit later when we had 30, 35 points.

"Now the situation is different. This situation will define us as well as a team, as a club, with our fans, with staff – we'll stick together and be combative until the end."

Our first #UEL defeat. https://t.co/0o8q7RHsOr

— Sunderland AFC (@SunderlandAFC) November 5, 2026

Sunderland were jeered by the Stadium of Light crowd at both half-time and full-time amid their worrying form.

Despite an improved second-half performance, which saw Sunderland limit Dinamo to just one off-target shot, while having 12 attempts at the other end, Le Bris' side were ultimately beaten by the damage done before the break.

"Tough period. We had two different halves," Le Bris said of the performance.

"The first one was difficult with many young players. This period is not easy to manage, and we felt even if they tried, it's heavy at the minute. It's not easy to change the dynamic.

"I appreciated the reaction in the second half, even though there were more experienced players. More quality, more experience on the pitch. We are unlucky because we created many chances, but it wasn't enough. It's like this: when you go on a poor run, it's hard to change the dynamic.

"We are still combative; the players tried until the end to show something different. We know that the most important game this week is at the end of the week against Chelsea.

"I'm pleased with the energy and competitiveness until the end. Now we need more quality; it's fair to say that, because at the minute, it's not the case."

Ferencvaros head coach Borbely Balazs insists that his side will come to San Siro and face AC Milan playing their way.

Having joined Ferencvaros from last season’s Hungarian title winners ETO Gyori, Balazs has made an excellent start to the campaign with his new club. They sit in third in their domestic league, two points off top but with a game in hand to be played.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

They have racked up 20 games unbeaten across all competitions, also winning three games out of three in the Europa League too. A 3-1 away win at Celtic was followed by home wins over Viktoria Plzen (2-1) and Torreense (4-1), making them one of the early pace-setters.

So, this is a big opportunity for the Fradi, who will be backed by around 5,000 away fans. The head coach of the Hungarian side – Borbely Balazs – spoke at a press conference last night at San Siro about tonight’s contest, and his words were relayed by MilanPress.

Do you remember your last time at San Siro?

“It’s been a long time: more than twenty years have passed since I was last lucky enough to play at San Siro. It’s a shame, however, that we had to play in front of empty stands back then.

“It was still a fantastic experience: we faced true world-class stars, like Materazzi, Adriano, and Luis Figo. Despite the four-goal defeat, it remains a fond memory.”

“I’m not someone who likes to look too far ahead. When the draw determined that we’d face both AC Milan and Juventus, I was struck by the fact that we were facing two giants of Italian football, clubs with immense traditions.

“However, we’ve prepared for every eventuality and arrived at San Siro with the right amount of confidence.”

“Our European campaign has been positive so far, but the match against Milan will be on a completely different level, even though we’ve faced strong opponents in recent months.

“The Rossoneri will likely retain possession more, so we’ll have to play with discipline, but we also need to be courageous when we attack.”

“My role model is Carlo Ancelotti. I’ve always followed the careers of Italian coaches. I’m Slovakian, and since several Slovakian players have played in Serie A, I’ve also kept an eye on their careers, as well as the coaches they’ve worked with.”

“It’s a source of great pride for all of us who represent Hungarian football.”

#1828. The Tottenham summer signing who is providing a surprise creative spark

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Roberto De Zerbi wanted three things above all else from Tottenham’s summer transfer window.

He needed wingers who could carry the ball over large distances, midfielders who could find diagonal passes into the feet of an attacker, and a ball-playing centre-back to partner Micky van de Ven.

It has taken some time to all fit together, but De Zerbi appears to have got what he wanted, with Spurs on their best run of form since February 2025 as £300million worth of new signings finally click into gear.

Tottenham’s historic win away at Chelsea was dominated by talk of Mateus Fernandes’ man-of-the-match display, while against 10-man Crystal Palace, centre-back Jan Paul van Hecke came to the fore.

Van Hecke has been a mainstay at the heart of Spurs’ defence since his £52m arrival from Brighton, and he is quickly developing a reputation as a confident and committed part of De Zerbi’s side.

His goal against Palace, which makes him the club’s top scorer in the league this season with two goals, had a bit of everything Tottenham supporters have come to expect from the Dutchman.

The determination to rise above Jaydee Canvot and power his initial header at Dean Henderson before reacting quickest, while on the floor, to nod in the rebound.

It was a scrappy finish but one that spoke to the newfound resilience within the Tottenham ranks. Van Hecke was one of the first names De Zerbi wanted to sign in the summer, and it is easy to see why.

His aggression in both boxes gives Spurs presence, while his comfort in possession - he completed a Premier League club-record 143 passes against Palace - provides a platform to build through the lines.

In James Maddison’s absence, Tottenham are still short of players who can pick passes in the final third, but with Van Hecke applying pressure and playing with purpose, they are able to sustain their momentum.

Spurs are unbeaten since returning from the October international break, and their performances have been characterised by an ability to swarm opponents and stay high, or play out of pressure by inviting overloads in build-up.

Van Hecke’s composure makes him adaptable, allowing him to remain an outlet in possession whether Tottenham are pushing high or inviting pressure from their opponents.

#1827. Former Man Utd chairman slams owners after controversial Avram Glazer comments

Former Manchester United chairman Martin Edwards expects supporters to be furious with Avram Glazer’s comments on the club and has accused the owners of getting their priorities wrong.

The Athletic report that Glazer made a controversial point while speaking to financiers at Deutsche Bank’s inaugural Sports Investment Conference in London in September.

One of the owners of the Red Devils compared Manchester United to the New York Yankees and Dallas Cowboys as a brand that will remain commercially successful irrespective of how well they are performing on the pitch.

Edwards, who was chairman of Manchester United from 1980-2003, expects fans to react badly to that sentiment and has encouraged the current owners to train all their focus on improving the team.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

‘I heard that this morning and I thought “By Jove, what’s the reaction going to be from the supporters?” Supporters don’t want to hear that!’ Edwards said on talkSPORT.

‘Supporters want to hear that you’re winning trophies. They’re not interested in profits or dividends or what people are taking out of the club. They want the club to be successful, they want the best players, they’d rather be spending money on the team than on the new stadium.’

Edwards accepts that running a club the size of Manchester United is a tricky business and owners must satisfy various stakeholders, but he feels the balance is currently off.

‘When I was running United, I always felt I had three responsibilities, really,’ he said. ‘One: in those days we were still developing the ground, so I had to build the ground and develop the ground. Look after the team, which is always the most important. But also, because we were public we had to pay dividends and keep the shareholders happy.

‘It’s a balance. Running a football club is a complete balance, from top to balance. It’s a question of whether you get it right or wrong.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

He added: ‘I think it’s quite clear, in my eyes, that the team is the most important element at the moment. You’ve got to get the team right and forget new stadiums if you’re not going to fill them. Get the team winning again and get the supporters behind you. We’re not a united front at the moment.’

The landscape of top flight football has changed considerably since Edwards was in charge at Manchester United and he believes it has not all been for the better.

‘You’ve got owners now who don’t attend games. They put somebody in charge, whatever else,’ he said. ‘Existing owners now, they wouldn’t know who’s in the team.

‘It’s become big business and what you can get out of it. The game has changed and for the older ones of us it’s disappointing, really, the direction it’s gone.’

Looking back to the start of Manchester United’s decline as a title-challenging force in the Premier League, Edwards suggests it was the loss of Alex Ferguson and CEO David Gill in 2013 and Ed Woodward being named as Gill’s replacement.

‘Once Alec and David Gill decided to leave in 2013, that was a huge blow to the club and they’ve never really recovered from that,’ he said.

‘If you wanted to be critical you’d say right from the beginning when they replaced David Gill, they replaced him with not a football man, but a merchant banker.

‘If you’ve got the top of the football chain who’s not converse with football, that does make it difficult. I think that once the mistakes start, they multiply.

‘Recruitment has been a big problem. Look at the players they’ve bought, some of them haven’t been up to the standard. Generally it snowballs. That’s been the problem.

‘Also, have United spent enough money to be able to compete at the top? Manchester City have had a huge advantage in the short-term because they haven’t been sticking to the rules and other people have. That’s given them a huge advantage, so we probably couldn’t have competed with them, but we could certainly have competed with Liverpool and Arsenal and whatever else.’

#1826. Will Manchester United sack Michael Carrick and who could replace him?

Michael Carrick’s position as Manchester United head coach remains under threat, as a sack decision looms with the focus shifting to this weekend’s Premier League clash against Aston Villa.

The pressure has been mounting on Carrick following a disappointing start to the season, with his side only out of the relegation zone by virtue of a superior goal difference to Crystal Palace.

While, Tuesday night’s comeback win over Roma in the Champions League allowed Carrick to survive another day in the Old Trafford hot-seat, the former Man United midfielder will be aware that he is not out of the woods just yet.

As reported by The Athletic last week, United hierarchy held talks about Carrick’s future as head coach following the 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth on October 25.

Carrick had been widely expected to be sacked at that point and then again after Man Utd were beaten 2-0 by Chelsea in the Premier League, a result that sent them crashing down the table.

However, it was agreed that Carrick would oversee the Roma and Aston Villa games before his situation would be reassessed prior to the international break.

Now, even though Carrick ended a nine-game run without a victory in thrilling fashion against Roma, pressure still remains as the first half performance on Tuesday night was a disaster and United could have easily found themselves three or four goals down at half time.

Of course, the second half did prove that the players are playing for Carrick, so much so that Matheus Cunha went overboard in getting himself sent-off after turning the game on its head with two quickfire goals.

There’s an argument that Man Utd now have some much-needed momentum, but you get the feeling only a win over Villa on Sunday will be enough to keep Carrick in the job.

After all, would a draw against Villa would be enough? That question may only be answered come full-time as there is a scenario where United go into the international break in the relegation zone and therefore Carrick’s position becomes untenable.

As per reports, Manchester United's football operations leadership, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox hold all the power with regards to Carrick’s future.

The pair were both in attendance at Stamford Bridge last weekend and at Old Trafford on Tuesday, amid reports of being involved in discussions over potential replacements.

Taking into account that Carrick held crisis talks with Berrada and Wilcox after the Bournemouth game, they would all - along with minority shareholder Sir Jim Ratcliffe - be expected to meet at Carrington following the Villa fixture.

Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann are leading contenders to replace Carrick if he was to be sacked as Man United head coach.

Furthermore, in a boost for Man Utd if they end up pursuing Howe, they will only have to pay Newcastle a compensation fee of £6million.

#1825. ‘Different level’ – William Gallas backs Arsenal star for Real Madrid transfer

William Gallas believes that William Saliba could be tempted to join Real Madrid if the Spanish giants tried to sign the Arsenal defender.

Saliba joined Arsenal in a £27m move from Saint-Etienne in 2019 and has gone on to establish himself as one of the best centre-backs in the league.

The Frenchman was an integral part of Mikel Arteta’s side that won the league title last season, forming a rock-solid partnership with Gabriel Magalhaes at the heart of Arsenal’s defence.

Saliba is under contract at Arsenal until 2030, signing a long-term deal in 2025 after he was heavily linked with Real Madrid.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

But Gallas still believes he is destined to play for Madrid, and said his fellow countryman would find it hard to turn down a move to a club of that stature.

‘Are Arsenal at a high enough level now that William Saliba would turn down Real Madrid if they came in for him?’ Gallas told SeatPick.

‘I know a lot of people will be mad about what I’m going to say right now but if we are talking about the history of both clubs, Real Madrid and Arsenal, then Real Madrid is Real Madrid. They are on a different level.’

‘The pressure is bigger there. The atmosphere around the club is different. Every game, the fans expect you to win. Every game, the fans expect you to have a great performance. Every season, the fans expect you to win La Liga or to win the Champions League, so it’s a different level.

‘For me, even if their performances at the moment are not the best, and even if they haven’t won the biggest trophies recently, Madrid is Madrid, and I’m telling you, any player who has the opportunity to go to Madrid, they will try to go there, and you can’t blame them. You couldn’t blame a player like Saliba if that is his decision.

‘Arsenal and Manchester United? They are still behind Barcelona and Real Madrid, even Manchester United still to this day because they have such a big history.

‘That’s why I think now with clubs like Arsenal, even if they had a good history in the past, what they are doing right now is rebuilding.

‘They are trying to tell their story again, and they are on the right track, but they are still behind Barcelona and Real Madrid.’

Saliba has not played a minute this campaign after suffering a back injury at the World Cup, but is now back in first-team training and closing in on a return.

Speaking recently about the Frenchman, Arteta said: ‘All the preparation has been done to measure all the loads and all the steps that he had to do to minimise that risk.

‘Now he’s in a really good place. He’s built the capacity that we needed, and now it’s about giving him minutes. He’s a centre-back, and when that’s the case, it’s not like an attacking midfielder or a nine that you can change.

‘A centre-back normally has to be able to play 90 minutes, and that’s why all the preparation that we’ve done to build him.’

Saliba was an unused substitute against Slavia Prague on Wednesday, but could be in line to feature against Hull City on Saturday after Ezri Konsa was forced off in the second half of their 2-1 win.

‘He is obviously playing a lot, he’s played so many games in the last few weeks,’ Arteta said of Konsa after Arsenal’s win in Prague.

‘He had some issues and we decided to take him off.’

#1824. Mainz 05 vs Bayern Munich - prediction, team news, lineups

By Lewis Nolan | 05 Nov 2026 22:48

Bayern Munich will hope to maintain their place at the top of the Bundesliga by beating hosts Mainz 05 on Saturday at Mewa Arena.

The Bavarians' tally of 18 points is the same as second-placed Borussia Dortmund, whose inferior goal difference keeps them behind heading into matchweek nine, whereas Mainz are ninth with 10 points.

Mainz's form has been dire, with the club losing four of their last five games in all competitions, including three of their past four league matches.

Manager Urs Fischer will be alarmed by the nature of his team's 4-1 defeat against Elversberg on October 30 given the victors led 3-0 by the interval and led 4-0 by the time they conceded in second-half stoppage time.

The club may be in ninth place, but only three points separate them from 16th-placed Union Berlin, who occupy the division's relegation playoff spot.

Matters will not get any easy for the hosts, who have to face the current top four in their next seven Bundesliga fixtures.

Die Nullfunfer are yet to win at home this season, with Mainz having taken one point from a possible 12 at Mewa Arena, and a loss on the weekend would be their fourth consecutive defeat at the stadium.

Bayern's clash is taking place at exactly the same time as Dortmund's with Elversberg, though they could have entered the weekend ahead of their title rivals on points had they beaten them at Allianz Arena on October 31.

The leaders were held to a 2-2 stalemate by BVB despite twice going ahead, but they conceded an 89th-minute equaliser to draw for the second time in four league games.

Vincent Kompany's side have now drawn four of their past eight matches in all competitions, a period in which they remained unbeaten, while they managed to win 2-0 against Atletico Madrid in the Champions League on Tuesday.

That clash was the Bavarians' eighth game of the campaign played on the road, and it was their fifth triumph in that time.

The club scored at least two goals in all but one of those matches, but it was also just their second clean sheet away from home this term.

Bayern's record against their hosts is predictably strong, with the visitors having won five of their past seven meetings with Mainz, only losing on one occasion.

Mainz will hope that centre-backs Danny da Costa, Fabio Gruber and Kacper Potulski are at their best, especially as they cannot call upon Dominik Kohr or Stefan Posch, the latter of whom is suspended after being sent off against Elversberg.

Using fewer than three midfielders in midfield could give far too much space to Bayern, so expect to see Jae-Sung Lee, Kaishu Sano and Nadiem Amiri start together on the weekend.

Bayern still have several key injuries in their squad, with forwards Luis Diaz (hamstring) and Serge Gnabry (hamstring) ruled out, while Jamal Musiala (hamstring) is a doubt.

There is no doubt about the selection of Harry Kane, who will be keen to celebrate his new contract with his fifth Bundesliga goal of the season, and he could be supported by an attacking cast of Michael Olise, Lennart Karl and Alphonso Davies.

Joshua Kimmich and Aleksandar Pavlovic are set to patrol the middle of the pitch ahead of centre-backs Dayot Upamecano and Kim Min-Jae.

As for the manager himself, Kompany is still taking an enforced break away from football following his collapse earlier in October that required a hospital visit, meaning assistant Rene Maric will lead the team once again.

Zentner; Da Costa, Gruber, Potulski; Caci, Lee, Sano, Amiri, Widmer; Tietz, Becker

Neuer; Laimer, Upamecano, Kim, Brown; Kimmich, Pavlovic; Olise, Karl, Davies; Kane

Bayern may have several injury issues to contend with, but Mainz have struggled considerably in recent weeks.

The visitors could enjoy a fruitful afternoon at Mewa Arena, and striker Kane will relish to opportunity to add to his tally.

#1823. How Alvaro Arbeloa sparked Fulham revival to save his job

Ex-Real Madrid boss had looked on the brink at Craven Cottage before timely resurgence, with work still to do

When Alvaro Arbeloa was reminded of Fulham’s torrid record at Villa Park, a little smile broke out across his face.

He knew his team, in drawing 1-1 with Unai Emery’s side, had shown further evidence they are on the right track and turning around a season that had started woefully.

Arbeloa was not a universally popular appointment at Craven Cottage and this time last month was a pretty good bet to become the first Premier League manager sacked this season.

The narrative has changed now. As one fan said, “from being one game from the sack to earning seven points from three games is a brilliant return”.

How much credit Arbeloa personally deserves for Fulham’s turnaround is up for debate, but that moment when the ex-Real Madrid manager imminently faced the chop never materialised.

Last month, when Fulham had lost to strugglers Sunderland, Crystal Palace and Ipswich, and still had zero league wins, the club’s owner Shahid Khan appeared to come out in support of Arbeloa ahead of the home game against Hull.

“We have been in every match, missing only the opportunities we've had to complete the task,” Khan said. “I believe those opportunities will soon be seized - especially if we have our supporters in full voice today and beyond.”

Fulham were 1-0 winners over Hull in a game where plenty of fans believed they were deserving of a more emphatic scoreline to match their dominance.

Another clean sheet followed - in a 1-0 win at Coventry - before that draw against a Villa team who were then second only to holders Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League table.

“We have proved that we can compete with anyone,” said Arbeloa.

And Fulham had needed to get to that point under the Spaniard, not only because Premier League survival will depend on it but also because that was precisely what Marco Silva’s team did so well across four seasons in the top-flight.

A little sprinkling of luck is always needed when rectifying a bad situation, and Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki dropping a corner over the goal line did feel like the fortunate moment in question at a club where the players, manager and backroom staff had all been feeling hopelessly down on their luck.

Arbeloa is known to still be annoyed by Fulham’s wastefulness in front of goal; they are the third-biggest underperformers in the league for xG. Missed chances has been the one binding thread throughout his time in charge.

We have proved that we can compete with anyone

New striker Gonzalo Garcia has had his fair share of woes in that area and patience is beginning to wear thin from a fanbase not known for knee-jerk reactions.

When the defeats were piling up, Arbeloa reminding people of his stature within the game was an ugly look. Ex-Real Madrid manager or not, he needed to deliver deeds, not words. Fulham have begun to.

Where he deserves credit is in adapting his system. “At least he is prepared to change his ideology,” Fulham’s record goalscorer Gordon Davies tells Standard Sport, “because we’ve had managers in the past who are only prepared to play Plan A.”

The high-intensity pressing Arbeloa insisted upon in those opening games was wholly at odds with how Silva’s Fulham had played and the squad looked unable to bridge the gap between what they knew and what the new manager wanted.

“It worried supporters, especially given that you have a new manager, new players, and in the first game of the new season give a goal away after 30 seconds,” Davies recalls.

Arbeloa softened, becoming more pragmatic and accepting that results and only results would save his job as he headed for the brink.

A kind run of fixtures did eventually get Fulham out of their hole, though the Cottagers’ distinct lack of a clinical edge remains a major problem and a potential obstacle to them realising their potential.

Because their underlying data is impressive. In the ‘expected Premier League table’, Opta’s model says Fulham, who in reality are 15th, ought to be eighth.

Fulham are more possession-based under their new manager, their attacking patterns more zippy and lively than at the end of Silva’s tenure, when some felt they were “stale”.

Silva was exceptional at judging which substitution to make and when, though - the area representing Arbeloa’s greatest shortcoming so far.

Centre-backs Calvin Bassey and David Affengruber have been among Arbeloa’s trustiest performers, while 19-year-old midfielder Josh King has come on immensely.

Statistically his displays this season are night and day compared with last term, and he is shouldering real responsibility for his age.

While they may face difficulty trying to keep hold of him in the long-term, he has no shortage of fondness for the club that made him, telling Standard Sport in an interview in April: “My personal ambitions will come - but I feel I do have a certain loyalty to Fulham.”

Hosting Newcastle on Saturday is huge: a winnable game before a fairly long run of tricky fixtures. The pressure eased, Fulham must now kick on.

#1822. Didier Deschamps responds to Manchester United approach

Manchester United have sounded out Didier Deschamps as a potential replacement for Michael Carrick, according to reports in France.

Carrick’s position at Old Trafford is under threat as United have registered just one win in their last 10 games.

United appeared to be on course for a fourth consecutive defeat on Tuesday night but Mateus Cunha’s late double in the second half sealed a 3-2 comeback victory over Roma in the Champions League.

Replacements for Carrick have already been considered with Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann, Antonio Conte and Unai Emery all on United’s shortlist.

FootMercato reports that United have also made an approach for Deschamps to discuss a potential move to Old Trafford.

However, the 58-year-old is said to have reservations about taking the job at United and is prepared to wait until next year for his next move.

Deschamps ended his 14-year stint as France’s head coach in the summer following their World Cup campaign.

The former Marseille, Juventus and Chelsea midfielder guided France to victory at the 2018 World Cup, while his side were beaten in the final by Argentina four years later.

#1821. Prediction: Fiorentina vs Juventus

One of Italian football’s most intense rivalries takes center stage on Sunday evening when Fiorentina host Juventus at the Stadio Franchi.

Both clubs have fallen short of expectations so far this season. Fiorentina are battling near the bottom of the table despite signs of improvement, while Juventus remain well outside the title picture and can ill afford many more domestic setbacks.

Fiorentina head into this clash in better spirits than they were a few weeks ago.

After enduring a miserable run of three consecutive defeats without scoring, the Viola have collected four points from their last two Serie A matches and appear to have found some attacking rhythm again. Their most recent outing produced an entertaining 4-2 victory away to Sassuolo, where Mateo Pellegrino, Alieu Njie and Franco Mastantuono all got on the scoresheet.

Despite those encouraging results, Fiorentina remain 16th in the standings with only eight points from their opening fixtures, highlighting how much work Paolo Vanoli still has to do after returning to the club.

The biggest concern remains their home form. Fiorentina have picked up only two points from five league games at the Stadio Franchi and are still searching for their first home victory of the season.

Mastantuono has emerged as a bright spot, scoring four league goals since arriving on loan from Real Madrid. Alongside Pellegrino and Njie, he will be tasked with troubling a Juventus defence that has been hampered by injuries throughout the campaign.

Injury problems continue for the hosts. Fabiano Parisi, Arthur Atta and Marin Pongracic are unavailable, while Luca Ranieri faces a late fitness test.

Juventus arrive in Florence carrying far more momentum in Europe than they have managed domestically.

Luciano Spalletti’s side secured another important Europa League victory in midweek, defeating AZ Alkmaar 2-1 thanks to goals from Randal Kolo Muani and Teun Koopmeiners. That success moved the Bianconeri closer to direct qualification for the knockout stages and continued an impressive European run.

Juventus have collected only 17 points from 10 league matches and currently sit seventh, trailing surprise leaders Lazio by a significant margin. Their inconsistency has raised questions about whether they can realistically challenge for the top four, let alone the title.

The visitors at least restored some confidence by defeating Napoli last weekend, but away form remains a concern. Juventus have lost two of their last four Serie A road games and have won only once in their last seven visits to the Stadio Franchi.

Spalletti’s selection options remain limited by injuries. Kenan Yildiz, Khephren Thuram, Francisco Conceicao, Kamil Grabara, Zeki Celik, Nico Gonzalez and Manuel Locatelli are all unavailable, while Weston McKennie remains a doubt.

That places additional pressure on Kolo Muani and Nick Woltemade to translate their encouraging European form into domestic productivity.

Fiorentina’s recent improvement suggests this will be far from a straightforward evening for Juventus, especially given the atmosphere that inevitably accompanies this rivalry.

However, the hosts’ inability to turn home performances into victories remains a major concern. Juventus have been inconsistent themselves, but they appear to possess slightly more quality in decisive moments, and their recent European performances indicate growing confidence.

Expect a fiercely contested contest with little separating the teams, but Juventus may have enough experience and attacking quality to edge a narrow win.

#1820. England carry out Cole Palmer medical checks as Thomas Tuchel considers calling up Chelsea star

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

England have made medical checks with Chelsea on Cole Palmer as Thomas Tuchel weighs up whether to call up the 24-year-old.

Tuchel has been considering whether to name Palmer in his England squad on Friday ahead of Nations League group-phase games against Croatia at Wembley next Thursday and Spain in Madrid next Sunday.

Palmer has scored three goals and contributed three assists in nine Premier League games for Chelsea so far this season but was left out of the England squad for the World Cup and has not played for his country since March.

He was initially named in Tuchel’s squad for the last international break but dropped out due to injury, with the England head coach frustrated as he concluded the Chelsea talisman misses “too many opportunities” to represent the Three Lions.

"For sure, it is a missed opportunity. It is another missed opportunity. He misses too many opportunities and I don’t blame him for it, it is just a fact,” Tuchel said. “He misses way too many camps.

“I can only judge what I witness in my team. For that, you have to be in camp. If you are not in camp there is a next level to impress that you cannot achieve, because you only can do it when you are actually with me and us on the pitch. So, yes, it is a missed opportunity.”

Palmer has just 14 caps for England at senior level despite having been the scorer of their only goal in the final of Euro 2024, which they lost to Spain. He has only scored one other goal for England besides that strike against Spain: a penalty in a friendly victory over Bosnia and Herzegovina also in 2024.

He has featured in only three of the 26 matches of Tuchel’s England tenure so far.

Palmer scored the second of Chelsea’s two goals last Saturday as they beat 10-man Manchester United in the Premier League.
